label: input token q during the original phase
explanation: Fires exactly when the input is the letter q at an original-phase step (dev P=R=1.0). Never fires on q fed back as input during the copy phase, on the delimiter, or on any other token. Magnitude falls with position: q at t=0 reaches the max (~2.88), while q at later positions (t~5-6) sits around 0.5-0.6 of max. Repeated q also drops (e.g. 1.0, 0.82, 0.70 for 1st, 2nd, 3rd q). Recall is perfect, so in_first is not needed for it to fire.

issues: Factual claims hold up. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99999, F1 0.99999, mass recall 1.0. The only miss is one copy-phase q with activation of about 0.00 of max, which is noise. There are no false positives.
On the dev split the feature fires 0 times on the delimiter and 0 times in the copy phase, so 'never fires on fed-back q' is correct apart from that one near-zero test step.
Magnitude claim is roughly right. Implied mean at t=5 compared with t=0 is (0.079/11086)/(0.202/16560), about 0.58 of the t=0 mean. The top examples show t=0 q at 1.00 of max.

Minor caveat: the 'repeated q weaker' claim is mixed up with position, since later q's also sit at later t. One example shows a q late in the sequence at only 0.27. This is a nuance about magnitude, not a gap in coverage.
No systematic gap in L, prev_tok, first_tok or in_count. The firing rate on original-phase q is flat at about 0.033 for every orig_idx and L, consistent with the predicate.
